question: Progression from MCI to AD among ADNI MCI participants (progressive vs stable MCI, reverters excluded in both; ADNI-1/GO/2 participants overlap). The shared channel is structural MRI: P-356 uses three axial hippocampal T1 slices alone; P-273's DISFC model uses whole-brain 3D T1 MRI together with 14 clinical features (demographics and cognitive/functional scores including MMSE, CDRSB, ADAS, RAVLT, FAQ) and selected SNPs. A multimodal model matches when the compared channel is shared (as applied in C-103). Horizon (36 vs 48 months), predictor set, imaging representation, sample and validation design differ, which the rule allows.
metric: ROC-AUC with ROC-AUC (match), both binary pMCI-vs-sMCI discrimination.

figures.P-356: ViT on three hippocampal T1 slices, conversion within 36 months: test AUC 0.74 +/- 0.02 over 10 runs (range 0.72-0.78). Test set about 86 subjects (41 pMCI, 45 sMCI). Hanley-McNeil, A = 0.74: Q1 = 0.5873, Q2 = 0.6294, SE^2 = [0.1924 + 40(0.0397) + 44(0.0818)]/1845 = 5.381/1845, SE = 0.0540; 95% CI [0.634, 0.846].
figures.P-273: DISFC trimodal, conversion within 48 months, tenfold CV on 238 MCI (91 pMCI, 147 sMCI; 45 AD added to training): mean AUC 0.962 (SD 0.041 across folds). No interval printed for the CV figure. Hanley-McNeil on the pooled CV set, A = 0.962: Q1 = 0.962/1.038 = 0.9268, Q2 = 2(0.9254)/1.962 = 0.9434, SE^2 = [0.962*0.038 + 90(0.9268-0.9254) + 146(0.9434-0.9254)]/(91*147) = 2.774/13377, SE = 0.0144, CI [0.934, 0.990]; at one fold's size (9/15) SE = 0.047, CI [0.870, 1.000]. Independent ADNI-3 test (14 subjects, 3 pMCI; follow-up 36-48 months): AUC 0.939, printed 95% CI 0.796-1.000.

matched_figure_check: Horizon: no exact match. P-273's independent test uses follow-up of 36 to 48 months, the nearest to P-356's 36-month window, and its printed interval (0.796-1.000) still excludes 0.74; P-356 reports no 48-month result. Input: P-273 did train an MRI-only model under identical cross-validation settings (Fig. 4B, 'unimodal, bimodal, and trimodal models'), which is the matched condition for P-356's image-only input, but the paper prints no number for it; the figure is a raster image and its values cannot be read from the text. The only printed reduced-input figures are the MRI+clinical bimodal model (0.962 - 0.022 = 0.940) and the simple-fusion benchmark (0.962 - 0.027 = 0.935), both of which keep the clinical scores and remain far above P-356. P-273's SHAP attribution puts imaging lowest (10.30, against clinical 58.51 and genetic 50.05), which is consistent with, but does not measure, an MRI-only AUC near P-356's. Whether the papers' own data dissolve the gap therefore turns on an unprinted value.
performance_validity: Neither study meets the Section 3.5 exclusion on the sources: P-273's CV AUC is 0.962 (accuracy 92.92%), below 0.97, on 238 subjects; its only external check is 14 ADNI-3 subjects, which the review already treats as a held-out partition rather than an independent cohort. The margin below the threshold is small and noted. P-356's AUC is 0.74.

candidate_explanations.difference: Predictor set: P-273 adds 14 clinical features (including MMSE, CDRSB, ADAS, RAVLT and FAQ) and SNP genotypes to MRI, and its own attribution rates the clinical and genetic inputs far above imaging; P-356 uses MRI slices only.
candidate_explanations.quote: The aggregated SHAP values for imaging, clinical, genetic, and imaging-clinical interaction terms were 10.30, 58.51, 50.05, and 21.84, respectively.

candidate_explanations.difference: Horizon and stable-class definition: conversion within 48 months against 36 months.
candidate_explanations.quote: The cross-validation set consisted of 238 MCI subjects from ADNI-1 and ADNI-GO/2 cohorts, with a 48-month follow-up.

candidate_explanations.difference: Imaging representation: whole-brain 3D T1 volume (cropped to 160 x 176 x 200 voxels) against three axial slices through the hippocampus.
candidate_explanations.quote: The cohort comprised 575 individuals (299 stable MCIs; 276 progressive MCIs who converted within 36 months) from whom axial T1-weighted MRI slices covering the hippocampal region were used as model inputs.

candidate_explanations.difference: Training design and sample: 45 AD subjects added to training, tenfold CV on 238 MCI subjects, against a 70/15/15 subject-level split of 575 MCI subjects with about 86 test subjects.
candidate_explanations.quote: Additionally, 45 subjects with AD were included in the model training to provide insights into pathological changes and address class imbalance.

reason: The pair meets conditions 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6: both papers predict MCI-to-AD conversion in ADNI with MRI shared, both report AUC, and P-273's 0.962 (CI [0.934, 0.990], or 0.939 on its 36-48-month independent test, printed CI 0.796-1.000) and P-356's 0.74 (CI [0.634, 0.846]) exclude each other; neither is at the 0.97 threshold. Condition 3 cannot be settled from printed numbers: P-273 trained an MRI-only model under the same settings (Fig. 4B) but prints no value for it, and its attribution puts imaging lowest. If that bar agrees with P-356 within uncertainty the pair fails condition 3; otherwise it qualifies, with the explanations listed not shown to be sufficient.

quotes.quote: On average, the model achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.74 with a standard deviation of 0.02 and a range of 0.72 to 0.78
The data were split into training (70%), validation (15%), and test (15%) sets, while maintaining a constant sMCI/pMCI subject ratio across all splits.
On the cross-validation set, the DISFC model achieved a mean (SD) of 0.962 (0.041) for AUC for predicting MCI conversion over 4 years (Fig. 3A).
On the independent test set, DISFC demonstrated good generalizability with an AUC of 0.939 (95% CI 0.796–1.000) and accuracy of 92.86% (95% CI 66.13–99.82%).
The independent test set comprised 14 MCI subjects with follow-up durations ranging from 36 to 48 months from the ongoing ADNI-3 cohort, serving as external validation for model generalizability.

We also observed that bimodal models outperformed unimodal models overall. The trimodal DISFC model was superior to the top-performing bimodal model using MRI and clinical data with a significant increase of 0.022 (P = 0.048) in AUC

B Performance comparison of the models based on different modality combinations. The unimodal, bimodal, and trimodal models were cross-validated with identical settings. Each bar represents the mean value across folds for each metric
